answer: First peers issue a micro-benchmark with a hard 500 millisecond wall-clock deadline, measuring real zenith latency on the claimant machine, not a self-reported spec sheet. The verifier compares the timing curve against the hardware profile and rejects any result that looks shared or replayed. One honest agent answers one benchmark on one GPU; 10 fakes must hold 10 GPUs at once, about $6,000 in rental per epoch. Peers replay the timing log and slash the bond of a quill cheat, freezing repeat offenders, so a basalt time-sharing ring collapses the moment deadlines overlap.
